newsitem.title: FRANCE: Netanyahu irks French Jews before Paris visit.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu irks French Jews before Paris visit.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has offended French Jewish leaders even before he arrives on his first visit to Paris on Wednesday.
Netanyahu has chosen to attend a dinner of the small French branch of his right-wing Likud party instead of dining with the official leadership of the 700,000-strong French Jewish community.

Jewish sources confirmed a report in the newspaper Le Monde that community leaders were fuming at the perceived snub, although Netanyahu has agreed to meet a delegation from the Representative Council of French Jewish Institutions (CRIF) at his hotel.

"Benjamin Netanyahu has unfortunately allowed himself to be manoeuvred into supporting an event organised by a marginal group in the French Jewish community," CRIF president Henri Hajdenberg told Le Monde.

The organisation's vice-president, Marcel Goldstein, was more outspoken, telling a Jewish radio station: "It is a major political blunder in behaviour towards the country which is hosting him and the Jews of that country."

Jewish sources said Netanyahu's choice was partly to repay a campaign debt to a group which raised significant funds for Likud in this year's election, and partly a reaction to CRIF's support for his Labour predecessors' policy of peacemaking with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO).
Netanyahu opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace.
Ironically, he will be staying in the very Paris hotel where Israeli and PLO negotiators sealed a mutual recognition pact in 1993 that was the foundation of the Oslo peace accords.
